title: Mana Tempest Guide — Mana Drain, Spell Empowerment, Split and Positioning
summary: Mana Tempest creates a stationary storm that drains your mana per second while active and empowers spells cast inside it with added lightning damage based on your mana. It is the core enabler for mana-stacking Oracle and Titan builds. This guide covers the drain math, what costs count, spell empowerment scope, Split, and how long the buff lingers after you leave.
description: Mana Tempest deep guide: mana drain per second, what raises the storm cost, Gain Damage as Lightning, Spell Empowerment scope, Split vs Chain/Fork, linger after leaving, quality, why the storm ends early, mana planning, Archmage interaction, mapping and boss usage, troubleshooting and community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Quick Answer
paragraphs: Mana Tempest drops a stationary storm. While it is up, it drains mana per second, and the cost goes up the more you cast inside it.
Spells cast inside the storm gain added Lightning Damage scaled by your maximum mana — this is the whole point of mana-stacking builds.
When you leave the storm, the empowerment lingers for a short time, so you can step out and keep benefiting briefly.

notes: Tagged spell, aura, lightning, mana, empower.

properties.label: Cost

properties.label: Best role
notes: Core for Oracle and Titan mana builds.

sections.title: Requirements
paragraphs: No special attribute gate. Mana Tempest is a spell gem; its value scales with maximum mana and mana regeneration, so a mana-stacking character gets the most from it.

sections.title: The Mana Storm
paragraphs: Activating Mana Tempest places a storm at your location. The storm has a base mana cost per second and a duration; while you stand in it and cast, the per-second cost climbs.
The storm ends early if your mana hits zero or the duration expires, so you must plan your mana pool and regeneration around the window you want to spend inside.
The empowerment is the reason to tolerate the drain: spells cast inside gain Lightning Damage as a fraction of your maximum mana.
bullets: Base cost per second plus a scaling cost from casting.
Ends on mana depletion or duration expiry.
Empowerment is the payoff for the drain.

sections.title: Spell Empowerment Scope
paragraphs: Spells you cast while inside the storm gain a portion of your maximum mana as added Lightning Damage. This is why mana-stacking builds funnel every point of maximum mana they can.
Weapon innate skills that cost no mana can still be empowered if they are spells cast inside the storm — the empowerment is about where you cast, not whether the spell costs mana.
Triggered spells cast from inside the storm are also empowered, which is how a triggered Spark or Comet benefits from the tempest.
bullets: Empowerment scales with maximum mana.
No-mana spells still benefit if cast inside.
Triggered spells inside are empowered too.

sections.title: Split vs Chain / Fork
paragraphs: Mana Tempest's Split is a distinct behaviour from Chain or Fork. Split creates additional projectile paths from the cast, while Chain and Fork are their own support behaviours.
If a spell already has Chain or Fork, Split stacks as a separate source of extra projectiles, which can multiply screen coverage inside the storm.
Do not assume Split obeys the same targeting rules as Chain; treat it as its own layer.
bullets: Split is separate from Chain and Fork.
It can stack with those supports for more projectiles.
Targeting rules differ from Chain.

sections.title: Linger and Positioning
paragraphs: After you step out of the storm, the empowerment lingers for a short time, letting you reposition or dodge while still dealing empowered spells.
Place the storm where you will fight, not where you enter. In boss fights, drop it on the boss arena centre so your casts stay empowered during the dance.
In maps, you rarely want to stop and stand; drop the storm, cast a burst, and move on before the drain bites.
bullets: Empowerment lingers briefly after leaving.
Place the storm on the fight, not the entry.
Maps: burst then move to avoid heavy drain.

sections.title: Support Compatibility
paragraphs: Mana Tempest itself is an aura-like spell; supports that help spell auras or duration apply. The spells you cast inside benefit from their own supports.
bullets: Increased Duration helps the storm stay up.
Spell supports apply to the empowered payloads.
Mana-related supports help the caster survive the drain.

sections.title: Support Loadouts
paragraphs: For the tempest gem, duration and mana-efficiency supports keep the storm alive. For the payload spells, use lightning and crit supports as normal.
bullets: Tempest: Increased Duration, mana efficiency.
Payload: Lightning Damage, Crit, Penetration.
Quality often adds empowerment or duration.

sections.title: Skill Interactions
paragraphs: Mana Tempest empowers Spark, Comet and Eye of Winter cast inside it, making it the hub of mana-stacking caster setups.
Archmage-style mana scaling raises both your mana pool (more empowerment) and spell cost, so the storm drains faster — you must balance investment with regeneration.
Triggered spells from a cast-on-crit setup still count as cast inside the storm if the trigger fires while you stand in it.
bullets: Empowers Spark, Comet, Eye of Winter.
Archmage raises empowerment but also drain.
Triggered spells inside are empowered.

sections.title: Mapping Usage
paragraphs: In maps, dropping the storm and standing still is usually a trap. Use it as a burst window: place it, cast your screen-clear spell a few times, then leave.
The linger means your next few casts after stepping out stay empowered, smoothing the transition back to movement.
bullets: Burst inside, then move.
Use the linger for the exit casts.
Do not camp the storm in maps.

sections.title: Bossing Rotation
paragraphs: Against a boss, drop the storm at the start of the fight or during a stationary phase, then cast your empowered single-target spell through the window.
Time the storm for when you can actually stand and cast; during heavy movement phases, skip it and rely on the linger from earlier.
bullets: Drop storm on fight start or a still phase.
Cast empowered Comet through the window.
Skip during heavy movement; use linger.

sections.title: Build Usage
paragraphs: Mana Tempest is the signature enabler for mana-stacking Oracle and Titan caster builds, where maximum mana is pushed as high as possible.
It pairs naturally with Spark and Comet as the empowered payloads in the same setup.
bullets: Mana-stacking Oracle: tempest plus totems.
Twisted Empyrean mana Titan: tempest plus spells.
Spark / Comet as empowered payloads.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: If the storm ends early, your mana is depleting — raise regeneration or cast less inside. If empowerment feels weak, your maximum mana is too low for the build.
If Archmage seems to empty you faster, that is expected; add mana regen or flask sustain.
bullets: Storm ends early: mana depletion, add regen.
Weak empowerment: raise maximum mana.
Archmage drains fast: balance with sustain.
No benefit outside storm: cast inside it.
Linger expired: re-enter or re-drop.

sections.title: Community Evidence
paragraphs: Mana-stacking Oracle and Titan builds featuring Mana Tempest are repeatedly highlighted in 0.5 meta threads as high-ceiling caster setups.
The main community caution is the mana drain: players warn that without regeneration the storm is a liability.
bullets: Tempest Oracle / Titan are 0.5 meta picks.
Drain without regen is the common failure.
